summary: Range lights on Daufuskie Island's Calibogue Sound, lit 1873 and discontinued by 1924; the rear light is now a guest house in the private Haig Point community.

lens.note: Rear light: fifth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends). Front light: steamer lens.

structures.material: wood (two-story frame house with tower on the roof)

structures.note: On rails so it could follow the shifting entrance; no source read says what became of it

staffing.note: Keepers Comer, Stonebridge, and Sisson; discontinued 1924

access.note: Owned by the Haig Point community; reached by boat; grounds, dwelling and tower closed to the public

stay.note: Guest accommodation for Haig Point community members; since 2019 a stay can be part of a Haig Point discovery experience

events.note: Two range lights and keeper's dwelling built (contract December 1872 for $7,681)
Lit for the first time 1 October 1873 (LighthouseFriends)
A dock added to the station (LighthouseFriends; a boathouse and ramp followed in 1875)
Earthquake of 31 August 1886: plaster fell, the clock stopped at 9:25 p.m. (LighthouseFriends)
Storm of late August 1893: front beacon and wharves at Daufuskie damaged; long wharves needed rebuilding

Keeper Richard Stonebridge assists two occupants of a disabled launch; named in the Commissioner's report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1922 (July 1921 to June 1922); the day is not given (Commissioner's report)
Two lights changed to fixed-to-flashing and from oil to acetylene (1924 bulletin)
Station discontinued a year after Stonebridge's retirement (LighthouseFriends). The USLHS keeper roster ends with Sisson in 1924; the place record gives no discontinuance date.
Government sells lighthouse and five acres at sealed bid to a Savannah buyer for $1,499.99
Bought by a private owner, who repaired it (LighthouseFriends)
Repairs reported in a 1967 Beaufort County newspaper (quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Part of the Daufuskie Island Historic District, NRHP 82003831 (contributing property)
International Paper Realty Corporation purchases Haig Point (LighthouseFriends)

corrections.why: The rear light was first lit on 1 October 1873 (LighthouseFriends). The 1987 entry is the private re-lighting: 18 October 1986 per LighthouseFriends.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1987 'first_lit' is a later relighting. The light was first lit in 1873 and relit in 1986 as a private aid after a restoration (LighthouseFriends).

notes_for_editor: Deactivation date: the archive and LighthouseFriends give 1922-1924 (Stonebridge retired 1 July 1923 per LighthouseFriends; the archive roster says principal keeper to 1922; Sisson's stint runs to 1924). The 1924 bulletin records the lights changed to flashing and acetylene that year. The USLHS place record gives no discontinuance year; an earlier draft said the archive did, and that was removed. Some sources cited by Wikipedia give 1934 or 1938; those are not confirmed here. The 1922 rescue is in the Commissioner's report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1922 (July 1921 to June 1922); the record's 1922 event year is that report's year, not a confirmed day. Front light: the record lists it as standing. No source read says what became of the wooden front light after the station closed; the story says so. Focal height: the record's 5.2 m is the front light's height. The rear light's focal plane is 65 ft (LighthouseFriends), about 19.8 m. Status: the record says inactive. The rear light was relit in 1986 as a private aid (LighthouseFriends). Bridget Comer: the roster gives 1873-1885; LighthouseFriends calls her his assistant and spells the name Bridgett. The 1864 rules restrict women's employment in managing lights unless the department gives special authority; no source read says whether it did, and the story presents those rules as general context only. Stonebridge: LighthouseFriends (retired 1 July 1923) and the roster (principal to 1922) disagree; both are given. Two names overlap with the Morris Island roster (Richard Stonebridge, Charles L. Sisson). The archive gives both Haig lines and the Morris lines the same person slugs (richard-stonebridge, charles-l-sisson). The Morris roster has Stonebridge as assistant 1886-1891 and Sisson as assistant 1907-1908 and principal 1912-1913, so a move from Morris to Haig is possible, but no source read here connects them. The editor should check the archive's person pages before the keepers index joins them. Names matched by column position: none. Wikipedia is not cited. The owner's haigpoint.com page is not counted as a separate source.
